ARI.brief: Jacoby Brissett opens as the starter after a surprise 2025 in which he averaged 18.9 fantasy points across 12 starts; rookie Carson Beck is behind him. Rookie RB Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has a high-ankle sprain and Arizona is only hopeful for Week 1, which pushes Tyler Allgeier toward early lead-back work. James Conner is still not cleared for 11-on-11 work coming off last year's foot injury. Trey McBride remains the offense's true focal point regardless of who is at quarterback.

ATL.brief: Kevin Stefanski takes over as head coach and Tua Tagovailoa signed to start, with Michael Penix Jr. still limited to 7-on-7 work while rehabbing his knee. The backfield stays Bijan Robinson's with Brian Robinson Jr. added as the change-of-pace. Drake London is the clear No. 1 receiver and Kyle Pitts is coming off the best season of his career. Rookie Zachariah Branch and Jahan Dotson round out a thin receiver room behind London.

BAL.brief: Jesse Minter is the new head coach with Declan Doyle calling plays, a full staff turnover around a mostly intact roster. Lamar Jackson is healthy after an injury-marred 2025 and Derrick Henry is expected to keep a heavy workload with more passing-game work than in past years. Zay Flowers has taken over as the primary target while Mark Andrews' usage has declined two years running. Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane and RB Adam Randall have both flashed in the preseason.

BUF.brief: Joe Brady returns as playcaller and the Bills finally added a true No. 1 receiver in DJ Moore, who has been building chemistry with Josh Allen since the spring. James Cook is coming off a league-leading 1,621 rushing yards and the staff has hinted at expanding his receiving role. Keon Coleman is in a walking boot on his right foot after being hurt in the preseason opener. Khalil Shakir and Dalton Kincaid remain the complementary targets.

CAR.brief: Dave Canales' offense runs through Bryce Young, who has still not produced a fantasy-relevant season in three tries. Chuba Hubbard is week-to-week with a hamstring injury, though Canales says he is confident Hubbard is available for Week 1, leaving Jonathon Brooks as the primary alternative. Tetairoa McMillan is coming off Offensive Rookie of the Year honors and is the unquestioned No. 1 receiver. Carolina signed Darren Waller in mid-August to a one-year deal and is easing him in.

CHI.brief: Ben Johnson's offense enters Year 2 with Caleb Williams coming off a big statistical leap and a young trio of Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland. Loveland closed 2025 with four straight games of double-digit targets, the clearest signal of where the passing game is trending. D'Andre Swift has had a standout camp; backup Kyle Monangai hyperextended his right knee and is expected out multiple weeks. Pace and volume should stay high in a scheme built to feed the middle of the field.

CIN.brief: Joe Burrow is back from the injury that cost him nine games in 2025 and the Bengals are installing a new offense under Zac Taylor's revised staff, with camp reports describing steady progress. Chase Brown is the workhorse after a huge close to 2025 and has been taking reps split out wide. Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins remain intact as one of the league's best receiver duos. Tight end is an afterthought here with Mike Gesicki nominally atop the depth chart.

CLE.brief: Deshaun Watson opened camp ahead of Shedeur Sanders and started the preseason opener, but Cleveland has scheduled Sanders to start the second game, so the job is unsettled. Quinshon Judkins is the lead back and is expected to take on more passing-game work. Harold Fannin Jr. broke out as a rookie and is the top target. First-round rookie KC Concepcion and second-rounder Denzel Boston join Jerry Jeudy in a rebuilt receiver room.

DAL.brief: Dak Prescott led the NFL in completions in 2025 and returns with CeeDee Lamb and franchise-tagged George Pickens, one of the league's better pass-catching pairs. Javonte Williams re-signed after a career year and is the lead back. Jake Ferguson is coming off a career season but has slipped in some rankings. The offense remains pass-first under Brian Schottenheimer with little rushing contribution from the quarterback.

DEN.brief: Davis Webb is the new playcaller and Denver traded for Jaylen Waddle to pair with Courtland Sutton. Bo Nix has finished seventh among quarterbacks in each of his two seasons on the strength of his rushing. The backfield is a genuine competition between J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey with rookie Jonah Coleman pushing for a share. Evan Engram was a nonfactor in his first Denver season and the tight end spot is low-priority.

DET.brief: Jared Goff returns for his sixth season in Detroit behind an offense that still produces high volume but almost no quarterback rushing. Jahmyr Gibbs is the centerpiece; Isiah Pacheco was signed and is dealing with an MCL issue. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams are both back, with Williams managing a minor shoulder injury. Dan Campbell has called this the best receiver room he has had, with Isaac TeSlaa the favorite for No. 3 duties.

GB.brief: Jordan Love has graded out as one of the league's better passers but has not converted that into fantasy production. Josh Jacobs is working back from a groin injury and could return to practice soon; MarShawn Lloyd is the primary insurance. Tucker Kraft is back from a torn ACL and has said he expects a snap count roughly until midseason. Christian Watson and Jayden Reed lead a receiver room that lost Dontayvion Wicks to Philadelphia.

HOU.brief: C.J. Stroud enters Year 4 with his passing production having declined every season, and Houston traded for David Montgomery to stabilize the run game. Nico Collins is the clear No. 1 receiver with second-year Jayden Higgins opposite him. Alec Pierce is on PUP with an ankle injury but the Colts, not Houston, hold his rights - Houston's depth concern is Jaylin Noel, who is dealing with a hamstring but is expected back for Week 1. Tank Dell is still working back at his own pace from the 2024 knee injury.

IND.brief: Daniel Jones re-signed after a strong first season in Indianapolis and Shane Steichen's offense returns mostly intact. Jonathan Taylor led the NFL in carries and touchdowns in 2025 and is the engine. Alec Pierce is on PUP with an ankle injury but the team expects him for Week 1. Tyler Warren's rookie production was directly tied to Jones being healthy, and Indianapolis added Keenan Allen on a one-year deal in mid-August.

JAX.brief: Liam Coen returns as playcaller with Trevor Lawrence coming off the best season of his career. The backfield is unsettled: Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. are listed as co-starters and LeQuint Allen is out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury. Brian Thomas Jr. is being deployed as the X receiver and Parker Washington is a breakout candidate but is day-to-day. Travis Hunter has been listed as a starting cornerback and second-string receiver, a meaningful change to his fantasy outlook.

KC.brief: Patrick Mahomes is recovering from a torn ACL suffered in Week 15 and did not play in the preseason opener; Andy Reid has not committed to his Week 1 status. Kenneth Walker III signed as the feature back after winning Super Bowl MVP. Rashee Rice is not expected to face further league discipline and is the top receiver, with Xavier Worthy managing a shoulder issue. Travis Kelce returns for what may be a final season after his lowest target share since 2014.

LAC.brief: Mike McDaniel is the new offensive coordinator and has said he will use a hot-hand approach at running back, though Omarion Hampton is the clear lead. Justin Herbert has a healthy Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater in front of him for the first time in years. Ladd McConkey is the primary target after a down second season. The Chargers added David Njoku behind rookie standout Oronde Gadsden II at tight end.

LAR.brief: Sean McVay's offense returns the reigning MVP in Matthew Stafford, who led the league in passing yards and touchdowns. Puka Nacua has a groin injury and McVay said he may not practice at all this week, which is the single most important situation on this roster. Davante Adams remains the red-zone target. Kyren Williams is the workhorse with Blake Corum, who teammates say looks leaner and more explosive, behind him.

LV.brief: Klint Kubiak's first season features a quarterback competition between No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza and Kirk Cousins, with Kubiak calling the job Cousins' to lose while Mendoza has impressed in preseason. Ashton Jeanty is the workhorse back entering Year 2. Brock Bowers is the focal point of the passing game. The receiver room is unsettled behind Tre Tucker, with Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and rookie Mike Washington competing.

MIA.brief: Miami turned the offense over to Malik Willis, who has almost no starting experience but was efficient in relief work in Green Bay, with Jeff Hafley now the head coach. De'Von Achane is the centerpiece and Hafley has floated 40-touch games. The receiver room is thin after Jaylen Waddle was traded, with Malik Washington in the slot and Jalen Tolbert and rookie Chris Bell competing outside. Greg Dulcich is atop the tight end depth chart, which is itself a signal about the room.

MIN.brief: Kyler Murray beat out J.J. McCarthy and was named the Week 1 starter, a meaningful upgrade for the entire passing game after Minnesota's 2025 quarterback problems. Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison return with T.J. Hockenson at tight end. The backfield is a committee between 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason. Murray's rushing floor also changes the red-zone math for the skill players around him.

NE.brief: Drake Maye is coming off an MVP-runner-up season and the Patriots traded for A.J. Brown in June, giving him a legitimate No. 1 receiver. The backfield is projected as close to an even split between TreVeyon Henderson and Rhamondre Stevenson. Romeo Doubs and Kayshon Boutte fill out the receiver room and Hunter Henry remains a reliable red-zone target. The schedule is tougher than last season's.

NO.brief: Kellen Moore enters Year 2 with Tyler Shough, who broke out over the second half of 2025 and returns as the starter. Travis Etienne Jr. signed and is listed as a co-RB1 with Alvin Kamara, whose future is uncertain at 31. Chris Olave is coming off a career year. Rookie No. 8 pick Jordyn Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months with a hamstring injury, which elevates Devaughn Vele to the No. 2 receiver role.

NYG.brief: John Harbaugh is the new head coach with Matt Nagy calling plays around second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart, whose rushing production was elite as a rookie. Malik Nabers logged his first 11-on-11 reps in a red non-contact jersey coming off a torn ACL. Cam Skattebo is the lead back with Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary behind him. New York added Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney and has worked out free agent Najee Harris.

NYJ.brief: Aaron Glenn's second season starts with Geno Smith at quarterback after a trade from Las Vegas; he was a full participant Monday after an ankle issue. Breece Hall was franchise-tagged and sustained a groin strain Monday that the team has called minor. Garrett Wilson missed a day with a stomach bug and returned Tuesday. First-round rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. and rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq, who is working on a side field with a hernia, join a young pass-catching group.

PHI.brief: Sean Mannion is the new playcaller and Philadelphia moved on from A.J. Brown, leaving DeVonta Smith as the clear No. 1 receiver; Smith is working back from a hamstring injury. Jalen Hurts' rushing volume collapsed in 2025 and getting it back is the biggest swing factor for this offense. Saquon Barkley is looking to rebound from a down year. First-round rookie Makai Lemon is sidelined with a hamstring and Dallas Goedert faces obvious touchdown regression.

PIT.brief: Mike McCarthy is reunited with Aaron Rodgers for a second Pittsburgh season. Both starting receivers are banged up: DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. were both described as hard pressed to practice in mid-August. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle form a real two-man backfield after Dowdle signed. Second-round rookie Germie Bernard has taken advantage of the preseason reps.

SEA.brief: Brian Fleury is the new offensive coordinator and Sam Darnold returns after a season that was excellent in real terms but poor in fantasy terms. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the reigning Offensive Player of the Year and commanded a 36 percent target share. The backfield is thin: Zach Charbonnet is on PUP with a torn ACL and rookie first-rounder Jadarian Price is the projected lead back. Rashid Shaheed and Cooper Kupp fill out the supporting cast in a run-first offense.

SF.brief: Kyle Shanahan reloaded the receiver room with Mike Evans and a returning Deebo Samuel. Christian McCaffrey has missed practice time with tightness that has been described as not serious. George Kittle is on PUP with an Achilles injury but says he is very confident he will avoid the reserve list and has a chance for Week 1; Jake Tonges is the fallback. Brock Purdy is healthy after a nine-game 2025.

TB.brief: Zac Robinson is the new offensive coordinator with Baker Mayfield entering his fourth season as the starter. Bucky Irving is looking to rebound from a 3.40 yards-per-carry season and Kenny Gainwell was added after a strong second half in Pittsburgh. Emeka Egbuka is day-to-day to week-to-week with a toe sprain that the team has called stable. Chris Godwin is on the comeback trail after two injury-shortened seasons.

TEN.brief: Robert Saleh is the new head coach and Cam Ward enters Year 2 after taking a league-high 55 sacks as a rookie. Tennessee spent the fourth overall pick on WR Carnell Tate and added Wan'Dale Robinson, a real upgrade to the supporting cast. Tony Pollard has handled about two-thirds of the designed rushing attempts the past two years but missed practice in mid-August. Gunnar Helm takes over at tight end after Chig Okonkwo left in free agency.

WAS.brief: David Blough is the new playcaller with Jayden Daniels back from an injury-shortened season. Terry McLaurin is looking to rebound after both he and Daniels missed extended time, and Washington signed Stefon Diggs in August. The backfield belongs to Jacory Croskey-Merritt with Rachaad White added as the No. 2. Chig Okonkwo signed to take over at tight end.

4984.outlook: Unanimous QB1 across all seven sources and the only player in the file with a perfect 1.0 average. He has finished no worse than second among quarterbacks in six straight seasons and led the position in points per game in 2025 even in what was statistically his quietest year since 2019. Passing volume has dropped two years running, but the rushing floor is untouched - he has been top five among quarterbacks in carries and rushing touchdowns in all eight of his seasons. Joe Brady returns as playcaller and DJ Moore gives him the first legitimate No. 1 receiver of his career.
4984.watch: Nothing short of injury moves him; the upside case is whether Moore lifts his pass attempts back toward league average.

4881.outlook: Rebounding from an injury-marred 2025 in which he opened with three straight 26-point games, got hurt in Week 4 and averaged 13.5 points over his final nine. His scramble rate stayed high even while hurt, which suggests the rushing dip was health rather than decline. New head coach Jesse Minter and playcaller Declan Doyle are the variables; the supporting cast is otherwise the same one that led all quarterbacks in fantasy points in 2024. Sources are tightly clustered at QB2 with only ESPN and Fantasy Football Calculator down at QB3.
4881.watch: Confirmation in the first two weeks that the legs are back to 2024 volume.

11564.outlook: Trailed only Josh Allen in fantasy points, points per game and top-10 weeks in 2025 while leading the league in completion percentage and yards per attempt. New England traded for A.J. Brown in June, upgrading a supporting cast that was already good enough for an MVP runner-up finish. The schedule is meaningfully harder than last season's, which is the main argument for the small gap between him and Jackson. Camp reports have been strong, including a session in which he completed every pass in the first two periods.
11564.watch: Whether the tougher slate compresses his weekly ceiling, and how quickly the Brown connection develops.

6770.outlook: Back after injuries limited him to eight games in 2025, the third time in six seasons he has missed at least six. He was still a startable fantasy quarterback when active - a top-12 scorer in five of his final six games - but his ceiling is capped by essentially zero rushing production. Zac Taylor pulled back somewhat from his extreme pass-heavy approach last season, and the Bengals are installing new wrinkles that camp reporting describes as coming along well. Chase and Higgins are both healthy and intact.
6770.watch: Durability. Nothing about the talent or situation is in question; the games-played column is.

11566.outlook: Played only seven games in 2025 and was less dominant when healthy, at 16.3 points per game against 20.9 as a rookie, but the rushing usage held up at 58 carries in seven appearances. ESPN and NBC are the two most aggressive sources on him at QB2 and QB3; the CBS trio and FantasyPros sit him fifth or sixth. New playcaller David Blough and a receiver room that added Stefon Diggs in August are both unknowns. The dual-threat profile still gives him the highest weekly ceiling of any quarterback outside the top three.
11566.watch: Health, and whether Blough's scheme preserves the designed-run volume.

6904.outlook: Threw a career-high 25 touchdowns in 2025 but his rushing collapsed to 105 carries, 421 yards and eight scores after four straight seasons of at least 139 carries and 10 rushing touchdowns. That drop took him from three consecutive top-five finishes to eighth at 18.7 points per game. Sean Mannion is the new playcaller and A.J. Brown is gone, though the surrounding cast is still strong. Sources are tight on him at QB5 or QB6 except Fantasy Football Calculator at eight.
6904.watch: Tush-push and designed-run volume in the first month. If the carries come back, he is a top-three quarterback again.

3294.outlook: Led the NFL in completions in 2025 and has finished no worse than 11th among quarterbacks in all seven seasons he has played at least 16 games. His nine top-10 weeks tied for third at the position. He offers essentially nothing as a runner now, so the production is entirely volume-driven through CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Fantasy Football Calculator is the outlier at QB5 while FantasyPros has him 10th.
3294.watch: Age-33 durability - he has missed significant time in two of the past four seasons.

6797.outlook: Set career highs as a runner in 2025, finishing fifth among quarterbacks in carries and second in rushing yards, which is the main reason his outlook improved. His weekly production was volatile - five top-five weeks and nothing else better than 13th - and he has landed between 11th and 15th in points per game four years running. Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater are both healthy in front of him and Mike McDaniel is the new coordinator. Sources disagree sharply: CBS has him seventh, ESPN and Fantasy Football Calculator have him 14th.
6797.watch: Whether the McDaniel scheme raises his floor; he has been a ceiling-only quarterback for four years.

7523.outlook: Broke out in 2025, finishing no lower than seventh among quarterbacks in attempts, completions, yards and touchdowns while also placing top 10 in carries and rushing scores, and closed with seven straight top-10 weeks. His efficiency has never been better than fine, but the volume has been reliable - he has been top 10 in pass and rush attempts in each of his four full seasons. Liam Coen returns as playcaller with a deep group of pass catchers. NBC is a clear outlier at QB15 against a consensus around QB9.
7523.watch: Whether Travis Hunter's move to primarily defense thins the target group enough to matter.

11560.outlook: Took a real leap in Year 2, finishing no lower than 11th among quarterbacks in attempts, completions, passing yards, passing touchdowns, carries, rushing yards, rushing touchdowns and points per game. His completion percentage was among the league's worst at 58 percent, but he has thrown only seven interceptions in each of his two seasons. Ben Johnson's offense and a young trio of Odunze, Burden and Loveland give him room for another jump. FantasyPros is highest at QB7; ESPN is lowest at QB13.
11560.watch: Accuracy. If the completion rate climbs, he moves into the top six.

8183.outlook: Missed eight games in 2025 but was excellent when he played, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of nine appearances including three straight 26-point games in Weeks 15-17. He has quietly finished top 10 in points per game in each of the past three seasons. San Francisco added Mike Evans and brought back Deebo Samuel, and McCaffrey is healthy. Kittle's Achilles is the one soft spot in the supporting cast.
8183.watch: Games played. The per-game production has never been the issue.

12508.outlook: Delivered eight top-10 weeks as a rookie, tied for fifth most, despite taking the bulk of the snaps in only 12 games. The value is in his legs - he was top five among quarterbacks in rushing attempts, yards, touchdowns and carries inside the five. He went to the medical tent briefly in the preseason opener but returned and was cleared. New staff under John Harbaugh with Matt Nagy calling plays, plus a healthy Malik Nabers and additions in Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney.
12508.watch: His playing style invites contact; durability is the whole question with the upside already proven.

421.outlook: The reigning MVP led the NFL in passing yards and touchdowns and posted nine top-10 weeks, his first top-10 finish in points per game since 2019. Regression is the base case given he contributes nothing on the ground - one rushing touchdown since 2017 and 65 or fewer rushing yards in five straight seasons. Nacua and Adams are both back and the line is strong, so another big passing year is plausible. Fantasy Football Calculator is the outlier at QB7 against a consensus in the low teens.
421.watch: Puka Nacua's groin. Stafford's ceiling has always tracked Nacua's availability.

4046.outlook: Tore an ACL in Week 15 and is listed as questionable; Andy Reid ruled him out of the preseason opener and has not committed to Week 1. Before the injury he had an elite start to 2025 at 24.5 points per game through Week 8 and a poor finish at 15.0 over his last six. He gained ground as a rusher last season but that is exactly the part of his game most likely to be limited early in an ACL return. Sources are scattered from NBC at QB9 to CBS at QB17, which is the widest spread of any startable quarterback in the file.
4046.watch: Week 1 clearance, and whether he is allowed to run at all in the first month.

3163.outlook: Finished seventh, sixth and ninth in total points across the past three seasons, but his per-game finishes over that span were 15th, seventh and 12th - the season-long numbers are inflated by never missing games. He has never cleared 108 rushing yards in a season and managed 45 last year, which caps him as a fringe QB1. The Lions' passing volume and Amon-Ra St. Brown keep the floor high. CBS's Cummings is the high source at QB9; ESPN is lowest at QB18.
3163.watch: Nothing structural. He is a matchup and bye-week starter in 1QB and a fine QB2 in superflex.

11563.outlook: Has finished exactly seventh among quarterbacks in fantasy points in each of his first two seasons, entirely on the strength of his rushing, since his 6.5 career yards per attempt is poor. He posted 11 games of 15-plus points but only four top-10 weeks in 2025, which is the profile of a high-floor, low-ceiling starter. Davis Webb is the new playcaller and Denver traded for Jaylen Waddle. Coaches have praised his deep-ball accuracy in camp.
11563.watch: Whether Waddle and Webb raise the ceiling; the floor is already established.

5849.outlook: Named the Vikings' Week 1 starter on August 11, beating out J.J. McCarthy. Before a five-game, injury-wrecked 2025 he had finished each of his first six seasons as a top-12 quarterback in points per game, and his 2024 rushing line was 78 carries for 572 yards and five scores. He now gets Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson, comfortably the best supporting cast of his career. He is a bigger value in superflex than his QB17 consensus implies.
5849.watch: The Vikings' offensive line, which was the proximate cause of Minnesota's 2025 quarterback problems.

12545.outlook: Broke out over the second half of his rookie season, scoring 17-plus fantasy points in seven of nine full games including six straight to close the year, with 250 passing yards and 19 rushing yards per game. He never reached 22 points in a game, so the ceiling is unproven, but the supporting cast improves with Travis Etienne Jr. added. Rookie Jordyn Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months with a hamstring, which removes his most explosive intended target early. Kellen Moore returns for Year 2.
12545.watch: Whether the second-half production holds against a full season of defensive tape.

6804.outlook: Has finished ninth, fifth and third in QBR across three seasons as a starter without converting it into fantasy production, which is the whole story with him. Josh Jacobs' groin injury and Tucker Kraft's snap-count return from an ACL both limit the supporting cast early. Christian Watson and Jayden Reed are healthy but both have long injury histories. NBC is a strong outlier at QB12 against a consensus around QB19-20.
6804.watch: A jump in pass attempts. Green Bay has run a balanced offense that suppresses his volume.

4892.outlook: Three straight top-12 fantasy seasons, though 2025 was a step back - 12th in total points but 19th per game after finishing fourth in both in 2024. Zac Robinson is the new coordinator, which introduces real scheme uncertainty. Emeka Egbuka's toe and Chris Godwin's health history make the receiver room less stable than it looks on paper. He is expected to play in the second preseason game.
4892.watch: Egbuka's toe. Mayfield's 2025 slide tracked his receiver injuries closely.

8161.outlook: Signed with Miami and is set to start after two seasons backing up Jordan Love, where he was outstanding on a tiny sample - 70 completions on 89 attempts across two years. He has 155 career pass attempts, so the projection is almost entirely theoretical. He looked sharp in the preseason opener, going 4-of-5 for 43 yards with two carries. The receiver room is thin after Jaylen Waddle was traded, which caps the passing upside considerably.
8161.watch: Whether the efficiency survives a real starting workload; the sample behind his reputation is very small.

5870.outlook: Re-signed with Indianapolis after a strong first season in which he finished no lower than seventh in completion percentage and yards per attempt. He will not play at all in the preseason. Jonathan Taylor's workload and Shane Steichen's run-heavy tendencies cap his passing volume, which is why he lands as a QB2 despite good efficiency. Indianapolis added Keenan Allen in August behind Josh Downs and Alec Pierce.
5870.watch: Anthony Richardson's presence as the backup if Jones struggles early.

9758.outlook: Has seen his passing production decline in each season since a rookie year that produced 24 touchdowns and a ninth-place finish in points per game. He has not been a quality fantasy starter in two years and the sources agree tightly, all placing him between QB22 and QB24. Nico Collins is excellent and Jayden Higgins is a real second option, so the talent around him is not the problem. He is scheduled to play in the second preseason game.
9758.watch: A scheme or playcalling change; the personnel has been good enough and the production has not followed.

4943.outlook: Finished fifth in the NFL in passing yards for a second straight season and 27th in fantasy points, which is the cleanest illustration of why real-life success does not always translate. Seattle's run-first identity and his lack of rushing production put a hard cap on him. Brian Fleury is the new coordinator and Jaxon Smith-Njigba is coming off a 36 percent target share season. He is a matchup-only option in 1QB.
4943.watch: Whether Fleury opens up the passing volume; nothing else about his profile is likely to change.

3257.outlook: One of 2025's biggest surprises, reeling off nine straight top-12 weeks from Weeks 6 to 15 and averaging 18.9 points across 12 starts. He is again positioned as Arizona's probable Week 1 starter with rookie Carson Beck behind him. Trey McBride is the target that makes the whole thing work; Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson round out the group. He went 5-of-5 for 44 yards and a score in the preseason opener.
3257.watch: How long the job lasts. A rookie behind him plus a 33-year-old journeyman starter is not a stable arrangement.

12522.outlook: Was busy as a rookie - eighth in the league in dropbacks and attempts - but struggled to 5.9 yards per attempt and took a league-high 55 sacks. Robert Saleh's new staff and a supporting cast that added the fourth overall pick in Carnell Tate plus Wan'Dale Robinson give him a genuinely better environment. His preseason opener was uneven at 5-of-12 for 57 yards. Sources are clustered at QB25-27.
12522.watch: Sack rate. Fifty-five sacks is a pressure and processing problem that will cap everything else.

9228.outlook: Three seasons in and still without a top-20 finish in passing yards, a top-10 finish in rushing yards, or a finish better than 24th in points per game. His 2025 efficiency was a career low. Tetairoa McMillan is a legitimate No. 1 receiver, which is the strongest argument on his behalf. He was quiet in the preseason opener at 3-of-5 for 18 yards.
9228.watch: A step forward in efficiency. The volume has been there; the production has not.

1373.outlook: Traded to the Jets after an unsuccessful year in Las Vegas and is in line to start. He was a full participant Monday after an ankle issue. His fantasy peak was a ninth-place finish in points per game and he has not been close since. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell are the primary targets in a young pass-catching group.
1373.watch: Whether rookie Cade Klubnik forces the issue at any point in the season.

96.outlook: Re-signed with Pittsburgh at 42 and reunites with Mike McCarthy, who is now the head coach. He finished just outside the top 12 in passing yards and touchdowns in 2025. Both starting receivers, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr., were described as hard pressed to practice in mid-August, which is the immediate concern. He did not play in the preseason opener.
96.watch: Metcalf's and Pittman's availability in September, plus his own durability at 42.

6768.outlook: Signed with Atlanta after six seasons in Miami and his production and efficiency have declined every year since a 4,624-yard, 29-touchdown 2023. Kevin Stefanski is the new head coach. He has Drake London and Kyle Pitts, which is a real pass-catching foundation, but the receiver room thins out quickly behind them. He played two drives in the preseason opener.
6768.watch: Michael Penix Jr.'s knee. Penix is still limited to 7-on-7 but is the reason Tagovailoa's job is not secure.

13269.outlook: The No. 1 overall pick and reigning Heisman winner, a big pocket passer with the best off-target rate in his class at 7.1 percent. Klint Kubiak said the starting job is Kirk Cousins' to lose, but Mendoza threw a touchdown in the preseason opener and got reps with the starters. He offers little as a runner, which caps his fantasy ceiling even if he wins the job. His dynasty value is far ahead of his redraft value - he is QB15 in the dynasty superflex market against a QB31 consensus rank.
13269.watch: The Week 1 starter announcement. This is a straight either-or with Cousins.

4017.outlook: Expected back on the field after four lost years in Cleveland, where he has appeared in 19 total games and averaged 13.1 fantasy points. He started the preseason opener and looked sharp at 11-of-15 for 126 yards. Cleveland has Shedeur Sanders scheduled to start the second preseason game, so the competition is live. He was a top-six fantasy quarterback in each of his first four seasons, but that was six years and one major injury ago.
4017.watch: The Week 1 starter decision. Cleveland has not committed.

1166.outlook: Signed with Las Vegas and Klint Kubiak has called the job his to lose, with Mendoza pushing. He made eight starts for Atlanta in 2025 and averaged 12.5 points per game, reaching 18 only once. He offers nothing as a rusher. Even if he opens as the starter, he is a bench quarterback in superflex and undraftable in 1QB.
1166.watch: Whether he keeps the job past September; Mendoza is the long-term answer either way.

12524.outlook: Enters Year 2 competing with Deshaun Watson for the Browns' job. He made eight appearances as a rookie with eight all-purpose touchdowns, 10 interceptions and a 57 percent completion rate. He is scheduled to start the second preseason game after Watson started the first, so Cleveland is giving both a real look. Only three of seven sources ranked him at all.
12524.watch: The starting job. He has no standalone value without it.

11559.outlook: Still limited to 7-on-7 drills as of August 17 while rehabbing his knee, has not been cleared for 11-on-11 work, and missed the preseason opener. Atlanta signed Tua Tagovailoa, so he is no longer guaranteed a starting job. Across 14 career games he has 14 total touchdowns, a 21 percent off-target rate and a 60 percent completion rate. He avoids turnovers but contributes nothing as a runner.
11559.watch: Clearance for full team drills. Until that happens he is a stash, not a starter.

11565.outlook: Lost the Vikings' competition to Kyler Murray and is the backup. He appeared in 10 games in 2025 with 11 touchdowns against 12 interceptions and a 58 percent completion rate. He has said he wants to stay in Minnesota. His dynasty superflex value has fallen sharply, down 261 points over 30 days.
11565.watch: A Murray injury. That is the only path to relevance this season.

9221.outlook: The consensus RB1 with six of seven sources placing him first. He has finished top 10 among running backs in yards per carry, routes, targets, receptions, touchdowns and fantasy points in each of his three seasons, and his 38 touchdowns over the past two years are four more than any other player. The receiving usage is what separates him in full PPR - he has never been outside the top 10 at the position in targets. Detroit rested him in the preseason opener.
9221.watch: Nothing in his profile. Only a David Montgomery-style timeshare returning would change the picture, and Montgomery is now in Houston.

9509.outlook: Top five among running backs in carries, rushing yards, touches, total yards and fantasy points in each of the past two seasons, and no lower than fifth in routes, targets and receptions. Kevin Stefanski takes over as head coach, which is the only real variable. Brian Robinson Jr. was added as a change-of-pace but is not a threat to the workload. Fantasy Football Calculator has him RB1; everyone else has him second.
9509.watch: Stefanski's usage patterns in September. Everything else about the profile is settled.

6813.outlook: Improved in points per game in each of the past three years and delivered his best season since 2021, leading the NFL in carries and touchdowns while finishing second in carries inside the five. The touchdown volume is the entire case - his receiving work remains modest. Daniel Jones is back at quarterback and Shane Steichen's offense is built around him. He was rested in the preseason opener.
6813.watch: Touchdown regression. He led the league in scores on a workload that is hard to repeat at 27.

4034.outlook: Led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points in 2025, which makes him the highest-floor PPR asset at the position. His rushing efficiency was poor at 3.86 yards per carry, so the value is now almost entirely receiving-driven. He has missed practice with what Ian Rapoport described as tightness that is not considered serious. Turning 30 with a long injury history is why CBS's Eisenberg and Cummings both have him RB7 against an ESPN and FantasyPros RB3.
4034.watch: The tightness. Any practice absence that extends into September changes his September usage.

8138.outlook: Signed an extension and immediately posted the biggest workload of his career, finishing top five among backs in carries, rushing yards - a league-high 1,621 - touchdowns and yards per carry. The one limiter has been receiving volume, and Bills coordinator Pete Carmichael has explicitly declined to rule out a larger passing-game role in 2026. Ray Davis and Ty Johnson are the change-of-pace options behind him. Sources are tightly grouped at RB5-7.
8138.watch: Whether the pass-game work actually materializes; that is the difference between RB5 and RB2 in full PPR.

9226.outlook: Has scored 11 or 12 touchdowns in each of his three seasons and set a career high with 1,838 scrimmage yards in 2025. His receiving production has always been elite, which is exactly what full PPR rewards. Jeff Hafley said publicly that Achane may see games with 40 touches this year. Miami's quarterback situation under Malik Willis is the risk - defenses can load up if the passing game stalls.
9226.watch: Miami's offensive competence. His volume is safe; the scoring environment is not.

9224.outlook: His 2025 split in two: 10.1 points per game with one touchdown over the first seven games, then 21.2 points per game with 10 touchdowns down the stretch. Cincinnati is installing new offensive wrinkles and Brown has been taking reps split out wide, which points to expanded receiving usage. The CBS trio is far more aggressive on him than ESPN or NBC, who both have him RB11 against a CBS RB4-6. Joe Burrow returning is a clear positive for the scoring environment.
9224.watch: Whether the second-half touchdown rate was real or variance. The volume is secure either way.

12527.outlook: Enjoyed enormous volume as a rookie - seventh among backs in carries, targets and receptions - and graded eighth in forced missed tackle rate, but struggled with efficiency behind a poor line. Year 2 with Klint Kubiak's staff is the setup for a leap. He is the RB3 in the dynasty superflex market, well ahead of his redraft consensus, reflecting age-22 workhorse projection. FantasyPros and CBS's Eisenberg are highest at RB5.
12527.watch: Las Vegas' offensive line and quarterback resolution. The touches are guaranteed; the efficiency is not.

4866.outlook: Dropped from 2,283 yards and 15 touchdowns on 378 touches in 2024 to 1,413 yards and nine scores on 317 touches in 2025. He has been advocating for more plays under center, which is a real tell about how the Eagles' shotgun-heavy structure has affected him. Sean Mannion is the new playcaller. NBC is highest at RB6 while the CBS trio has him RB11-12.
4866.watch: Hurts' rushing volume. Barkley's efficiency drop and Hurts' collapsed carry total are the same problem.

8151.outlook: Signed with Kansas City after four seasons in Seattle and arrives as the reigning Super Bowl MVP and PFF's highest-graded back from 2025. He is positioned for feature-back duties in an Andy Reid offense after mostly splitting work last season. The Chiefs' backfield behind him - Demercado, Brashard Smith, rookie Emmett Johnson - is not a threat. His 30-day market trend is up 828 points in redraft, the largest gain of any back in the file.
8151.watch: Mahomes' Week 1 status. Walker's touchdown equity depends heavily on the offense functioning.

12507.outlook: Averaged 13.8 carries and 3.9 targets across nine appearances as a rookie, scored five touchdowns and finished 13th in points per game. Mike McDaniel, the new coordinator, said he will likely use a hot-hand approach in the backfield, which is the one caution, though McDaniel also singled out Hampton as having shown the most growth of any player. Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal are the change-of-pace options. The CBS trio is highest at RB8-9.
12507.watch: How literally McDaniel means the hot-hand comment. Hampton is the talent; the question is snap share.

3198.outlook: Finished second in the NFL in rushing yards for a fourth straight season at 32 and led the league with 24 carries inside the five. Reporting indicates he will keep his normal workload and be more involved in the passing game, which would address his one weakness in full PPR. Justice Hill is the passing-down back and Baltimore's new staff is the wildcard. The market has him at RB17 in dynasty superflex against RB12 in redraft, which is the age discount showing up.
3198.watch: Any sign of a snap-count reduction under the new staff. Age-32 backs rarely get advance warning.

13287.outlook: The No. 3 overall pick sustained a high-ankle sprain in the preseason and is unlikely to play again this preseason, though Arizona is hopeful for Week 1. He led the rookie class in yards per carry at 6.66 and yards after contact at 4.16 with a genuine three-down skill set. His redraft market value is down 602 points over 30 days on the injury. Tyler Allgeier is the direct beneficiary if he is not ready.
13287.watch: The ankle. High-ankle sprains routinely linger into the season even when a player is technically available.

8155.outlook: Franchise-tagged and sustained a groin strain in Monday's practice that the Jets and Connor Hughes have both characterized as minor. He has finished 17th and 21st in points per game the past two years in bad Jets offenses, a long way from his top-end rookie-contract form. Geno Smith is the upgrade at quarterback; Braelon Allen is behind him. Sources are tight at RB13-14 except CBS's Richard at RB20.
8155.watch: The groin, and whether the Jets' offense is finally good enough to support his talent.

8150.outlook: Three straight seasons of 1,350-plus scrimmage yards, including a career-high 1,533, and one of only 11 backs in NFL history with 13-plus touchdowns in three of four seasons. The touchdown dependency is the whole risk profile - the efficiency has never been good. Blake Corum is behind him and teammates have noted he looks leaner and more explosive. Camp reports on Williams have been positive.
8150.watch: Corum's snap share. Sean McVay has changed his mind about backfields before.

5850.outlook: His 2025 splits cleanly: 21.1 touches and 19.6 points per game with 11 touchdowns across his first nine games, then an injury. He is currently out with a groin injury; Matt LaFleur said he could potentially return to practice later this week. MarShawn Lloyd is the primary insurance and has been getting preseason starts. Green Bay's offense underuses its running backs as receivers, which caps the PPR ceiling.
5850.watch: The groin. He has been out since early camp and has not practiced.

7588.outlook: Re-signed with Dallas after finishing 12th among backs in 2025 with career bests in carries, rushing yards, touches at 287 and scrimmage yards. That was a genuine rebound after three poor seasons in Denver. The Cowboys' offense should score plenty with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens. Malik Davis is the only back behind him with any role.
7588.watch: Whether the 2025 efficiency was real or a product of volume; the Denver track record is a legitimate concern.

12481.outlook: Averaged 16.0 carries, 4.7 targets and 96.3 yards with six touchdowns across his six full games as a rookie before an injury ended the season. He started the preseason opener but warmed up with the second unit, which is worth watching. Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary are behind him. New York's new staff under John Harbaugh with Matt Nagy calling plays is an unknown.
12481.watch: Snap share in September. The second-unit warmup is the only wrinkle in an otherwise clean lead-back projection.

7543.outlook: Signed with New Orleans and is listed as a co-RB1 with Alvin Kamara on the first unofficial depth chart, which is the main reason his market value has dropped 572 points in redraft over 30 days. He has produced at least 1,399 scrimmage yards in three of the past four seasons and scored a career-high 13 touchdowns in 2025. Kamara's future at 31 is genuinely uncertain, which could resolve the split. He is capable as both a rusher and receiver.
7543.watch: Whether Kamara plays at all. If he retires or is phased out, Etienne is a clear RB2.

12512.outlook: Handled a massive workload during his healthy stretch as a rookie, bookended by an early absence for an off-field issue and a season-ending leg injury in Week 16. Reporting indicates he is expected to take on a larger passing-game role this year, which is the missing piece of his profile. Dylan Sampson is behind him. Cleveland's quarterback situation between Watson and Sanders caps the offense's ceiling.
12512.watch: The receiving role. If it materializes he is a low-end RB1; without it he is touchdown-dependent.

6790.outlook: Cleared 1,300 scrimmage yards in each of his first two Bears seasons, found the end zone 10 times and finished 17th among backs in 2025. He has been one of the standouts of Chicago's training camp. Kyle Monangai, who forced his way into a committee as a rookie, hyperextended his right knee and is expected out multiple weeks, which clarifies the early-season workload. Ben Johnson's offense supports back production.
6790.watch: Monangai's return timeline. Swift's value is highest in the weeks Monangai misses.

11584.outlook: Missed seven games and collapsed to 3.40 yards per carry in 2025, fourth worst among qualified backs, after a rookie year at 5.42 with 1,514 yards. Zac Robinson is the new coordinator and Irving has reportedly impressed him throughout camp. His redraft market value is down 715 points over 30 days, the steepest drop of any top-25 back. Kenny Gainwell was added and is a real threat for passing-down work.
11584.watch: Gainwell's role. Irving's rebound case requires him to keep three-down usage.

12490.outlook: Positioned to take over lead-back duties after Travis Etienne Jr. left, but is listed as a co-starter with Chris Rodriguez Jr. on the initial unofficial depth chart. He played sparingly as a rookie with 83 carries and 14 targets, clearing 10 touches only once. LeQuint Allen is out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury, which removes one competitor. Sources agree tightly at RB22-25.
12490.watch: The Rodriguez split. Jacksonville has not committed to a lead back.

5892.outlook: Traded to Houston after seven seasons in Chicago and Detroit, coming off career lows in touches at 182, yardage at 908 and points per game at 9.8. He caught an 80-yard wheel-route touchdown in camp, which reporting has framed as evidence of expanded passing-game involvement. Woody Marks is behind him after a 220-touch rookie season with poor efficiency. Houston's offense has been mediocre under Stroud for two years.
5892.watch: The Marks split, and whether Houston's offense is good enough to generate goal-line volume.

12529.outlook: Delivered three enormous games as a rookie, each over 28 fantasy points, but averaged 8.3 points in his other 14 while playing behind Rhamondre Stevenson. Chad Graff of The Athletic predicts a roughly even split with Stevenson this season, which is the central problem with his valuation. New England's offense should be very good with Drake Maye and A.J. Brown. The CBS trio is lowest on him at RB24-30.
12529.watch: Whether the split tilts. He is the more explosive back but has not won the job.

13286.outlook: The No. 32 overall pick and the projected lead back in Seattle with Kenneth Walker III gone and Zach Charbonnet on PUP with a torn ACL. He had only 280 career carries at Notre Dame behind Jeremiyah Love but posted the second-best YAC in his class at 4.13. He practiced fully Monday after a lower-body issue. George Holani is the main competition for early-down work.
13286.watch: Charbonnet's ACL recovery timeline, and whether Seattle trusts a rookie with a full workload.

5967.outlook: Has handled 67.2 percent of Tennessee's designed rushing attempts since arriving, at 15.2 per game, and still finished only 22nd and 30th in points per game because the offense has been bad and he has scored five touchdowns in each season. He was not spotted at Monday's practice with an undisclosed issue. He scored in the preseason opener. Robert Saleh's new staff and an upgraded receiver room could improve the scoring environment.
5967.watch: Touchdown volume. The carries have never been the problem.

8228.outlook: Set career highs in touches at 251, yardage at 1,291 and touchdowns at eight last season, finishing 19th among backs with 56 forced missed tackles, seventh-most. Pittsburgh signed Rico Dowdle, which creates a genuine two-man backfield rather than a clear lead. Both starting receivers are banged up, which could push more volume to the run game. Fantasy Football Calculator is highest at RB24.
8228.watch: The Dowdle split. Pittsburgh has two backs with similar 2025 production.

7611.outlook: Usually operated as New England's lead back last season and ranked fifth among backs in forced missed tackles, but Chad Graff projects a roughly even split with TreVeyon Henderson this year. He is listed second on the depth chart behind Henderson. The Patriots' offense should be strong, which makes even half of this backfield useful. Sources agree tightly at RB26-32.
7611.watch: Which back gets the goal-line work. That is the entire difference in this committee.

7021.outlook: Signed with Pittsburgh after nearly identical seasons with Dallas in 2024 and Carolina in 2025, producing about 1,350 yards and five to seven touchdowns on roughly 275 touches both years. He was effective at 4.57 yards per carry with 50 targets. Jaylen Warren is the incumbent and this is a real committee. He did not play in the preseason opener.
7021.watch: The Warren split. Dowdle has been productive in two straight seasons when given volume.

11583.outlook: Has appeared in one game since being drafted in the second round in 2024, having spent his rookie year recovering from a torn ACL and then re-injuring. He started the preseason opener and handled three carries and a catch. Chuba Hubbard is week-to-week with a hamstring, which is why the CBS trio has Brooks as high as RB26 while FantasyPros has him RB31 with an enormous standard deviation of 7.69 - the widest disagreement of any back inside the top 40. Carolina's offense is limited by Bryce Young.
11583.watch: Hubbard's hamstring. Brooks' entire near-term case is Hubbard being unavailable.

6806.outlook: Re-signed with Denver and is fending off RJ Harvey. In the 10 games both were active last season, Dobbins handled 153 carries at a 60 percent team share against Harvey's 50, but Harvey out-targeted him 29 to 15. He participated in Monday's practice after an undisclosed issue and did not play in the preseason opener. That target split is decisive in full PPR.
6806.watch: The passing-down role. Dobbins gets the early-down work but Harvey owns the receiving value.

7567.outlook: Signed with Tampa Bay after a genuine second-half breakout in Pittsburgh, averaging 13.3 touches, 85.0 yards and 17.8 fantasy points from Week 8 on across eight games. He is behind Bucky Irving, who is coming off an inefficient and injury-shortened season. ESPN is highest at RB31 while NBC has him RB40. He did not play in the preseason opener.
7567.watch: Irving's health. Gainwell is one of the better handcuffs in the league given his proven receiving usage.

12534.outlook: Hyperextended his right knee at Sunday's practice and is expected to be sidelined multiple weeks per Jeremy Fowler, after an MRI. As a rookie he played 41 percent of Chicago's snaps and averaged 4.6 yards per carry on 169 attempts, forcing his way into a committee with D'Andre Swift. The injury pushes his early-season value down substantially. NBC is highest at RB30.
12534.watch: The knee timeline. He was a legitimate committee back before this.

7594.outlook: Week-to-week with a hamstring injury, though Dave Canales said he is confident Hubbard will be available for Week 1. He is coming off a poor 2025 in which he lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle and ranked 64th of 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate. His redraft market value is down 615 points over 30 days. FantasyPros and Fantasy Football Calculator have him RB29-32 while the CBS trio has him RB39-42, a wide split.
7594.watch: The hamstring, and whether Jonathon Brooks takes the job while he is out.

12533.outlook: Played 39 percent of Washington's snaps as a rookie and finished 23rd among backs in rushing yards despite being a seventh-round pick. He is atop the depth chart with Rachaad White added as the No. 2. David Blough is the new playcaller and Jayden Daniels' return should improve the offense. The CBS trio is highest at RB31-34 against a FantasyPros RB40.
12533.watch: White's role. Washington signed a back with feature-back experience to back him up.

11586.outlook: Two seasons as Kyren Williams' backup with strong efficiency - 5.1 yards per carry last season, seventh among backs, and six touchdowns on 145 carries. Kyren Williams said Corum looks leaner and more explosive. NBC is a notable outlier at RB28 against a consensus in the mid-to-high 30s. He is one of the more valuable handcuffs given Williams' touchdown volume.
11586.watch: Any in-season shift in the Rams' backfield split; McVay has made abrupt changes before.

12489.outlook: Competing with J.K. Dobbins for Denver's lead role. In the 10 games both were active last season Harvey handled 50 carries and 29 targets against Dobbins' 153 and 15, which makes Harvey the passing-down back and the better full-PPR asset even in a split. Rookie Jonah Coleman is pushing for a share of the rotation. Fantasy Football Calculator is highest at RB31.
12489.watch: Whether he takes over early-down work. The receiving role is already his.

8136.outlook: Signed with Washington after four seasons in Tampa Bay, where he was a feature back in 2023 - top five among backs in touches, yards and points - and situational in his other three years. He is listed as the No. 2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. His receiving background makes him the more likely passing-down option. Sources agree tightly at RB36-41.
8136.watch: Whether Washington's committee tilts toward him on passing downs, which is where his PPR value lives.

8408.outlook: Back for a second Minnesota season, competing with 31-year-old Aaron Jones Sr. He was used often as a rusher at 9.9 carries per game but was a nonfactor as a receiver at 1.0 targets per game, which caps him badly in full PPR. He has had a productive camp. The CBS trio is highest at RB32-37.
8408.watch: Jones' health at 31. Mason is the early-down beneficiary but not the receiving one.

4199.outlook: Back for a third Minnesota season after an injury-plagued 2025 limited him to 747 yards, his fewest since 2017, and three touchdowns in 12 games. He is listed atop the depth chart ahead of Jordan Mason but this is a true committee at 31. Kyler Murray's arrival should improve the scoring environment. He played one series in the preseason opener.
4199.watch: Durability. He has not held up for a full season in some time.

10219.outlook: Listed as a co-starter with Bhayshul Tuten on Jacksonville's initial unofficial depth chart after three years in Washington, where he hit career highs in touches at 115. LeQuint Allen being out for the rest of camp with a soft-tissue injury simplifies the competition. He is a between-the-tackles back without meaningful receiving usage. Sources cluster at RB42-45.
10219.watch: Whether the co-starter listing survives into the regular season.

11655.outlook: Competing with Devin Singletary for work behind Cam Skattebo. He has produced 200-plus touches and 1,000-plus yards in each of his first two seasons, so the ability to handle volume is proven. He managed only two touches in the preseason opener. The Giants' new staff has not signaled a clear role for him.
11655.watch: A Skattebo injury. Tracy has the strongest track record of any backup in this backfield.

12474.outlook: Soaked up 220 touches as a rookie, 22nd among backs, but struggled badly with efficiency at 3.59 yards per carry. Houston traded for David Montgomery, which pushes Marks into a clear backup role. He did not play in the second preseason week. He does have receiving ability, which preserves some PPR floor.
12474.watch: Montgomery's health. Marks has already shown Houston will give him volume when needed.

9753.outlook: On the active PUP list with a torn ACL suffered in Seattle's playoff loss and remains in recovery mode as of the second preseason game. He would otherwise have been the clear lead back with Kenneth Walker III gone. FantasyPros has him RB47 with a standard deviation of 6.70, reflecting genuine uncertainty about his availability. Rookie Jadarian Price is currently ahead of him.
9753.watch: A return timeline. He is a stash, not a startable back, until Seattle clears him.

9508.outlook: Entering his fourth season as the change-of-pace behind Tony Pollard, a role that has produced nothing useful in fantasy. He was efficient in the preseason opener with five touches for 39 yards. Pollard missed a practice in mid-August with an undisclosed issue. Tennessee's offense should be better with Carnell Tate and Wan'Dale Robinson added.
9508.watch: Pollard's availability. Spears has never had a standalone role.

8132.outlook: Signed with Arizona and is directly in line to open as the primary back with rookie Jeremiyah Love dealing with a high-ankle sprain, per Adam Schefter. He totaled 1,174 yards on 226 touches as an Atlanta rookie but has not approached that since. James Conner is not yet cleared for 11-on-11 work. This is a short-term opportunity that Love's return would end.
8132.watch: Love's ankle. Allgeier's value is entirely a function of how many games Love misses.

4035.outlook: Entering his age-31 season with real uncertainty, including the possibility of retirement, though he is currently listed as a co-RB1 with Travis Etienne Jr. Over the past seven seasons his efficiency has declined steadily. New Orleans signed Etienne specifically to take over the lead role. FantasyPros has him RB49.
4035.watch: Whether he is on the roster in September. This is a roster-status question more than a usage one.

12469.outlook: Back for Year 2 in Cleveland after a rookie season in which his 2.69 yards per carry was dead last among 65 qualified backs on a small sample. He made an impact as a receiver in the preseason, catching both targets for 43 yards. Quinshon Judkins is well ahead of him. His path to value is passing-down work.
12469.watch: A Judkins injury. Sampson's receiving flashes are the only reason to hold him.

9511.outlook: Signed with the Chargers and will compete with Kimani Vidal for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. Mike McDaniel said Mitchell will have an offensive role on game days, which is a meaningful endorsement. He is an explosive but small back with a significant knee injury in his history. FantasyPros has him RB50 with a wide standard deviation.
9511.watch: How McDaniel deploys him. The hot-hand comment cuts both ways in this backfield.

8205.outlook: Signed with Detroit after four seasons in Kansas City, where he opened with 2,139 yards and 14 touchdowns in his first two years before injuries derailed him. He is dealing with an MCL issue. He sits behind Jahmyr Gibbs, which caps the role to early-down and short-yardage work. Detroit has no other established back.
8205.watch: The MCL, and whether Detroit gives him the goal-line work Gibbs does not take.

8154.outlook: Signed with Atlanta after a year as Christian McCaffrey's backup in San Francisco and will work as the change-of-pace behind Bijan Robinson. He is a downhill runner without meaningful receiving usage, which limits him badly in full PPR. He rushed twice for six yards in the preseason opener. Atlanta has no other back of note.
8154.watch: A Bijan Robinson injury. He has no standalone role otherwise.

11581.outlook: The primary insurance behind Josh Jacobs, who is currently out with a groin injury, and Lloyd has been getting preseason starts as a result. His NFL career has been almost entirely lost to injury to this point. FantasyPros has him RB56 with an enormous standard deviation of 11.29, the widest of any back in the file. He moved up seven spots since the previous refresh on Jacobs' absence.
11581.watch: Jacobs' groin. Lloyd is a pure contingency asset with a thin health record of his own.

13345.outlook: A fourth-round rookie who is trending toward a real role in a Denver rotation that also includes J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. He is a 220-pound back who was highly efficient across four college seasons at Arizona and Washington. His dynasty superflex value is up 147 points over 30 days. Three-way backfields rarely produce startable fantasy backs.
13345.watch: Whether Denver actually splits three ways or settles on two.

9225.outlook: Acquired by Philadelphia early in 2025 and worked up to primary backup duties, a role he is expected to keep. He sat out Monday's practice with a toe injury. Saquon Barkley's workload leaves little behind him in a normal week. The sample behind his efficiency reputation is small.
9225.watch: Barkley's health. Bigsby is the direct handcuff to one of the league's highest-volume backs.

13305.outlook: A fourth-round rookie with rare size-speed, running 4.33 at 6-foot-1 and 223 pounds. He impressed in the preseason opener with 63 yards on six carries plus a kick return. Ashton Jeanty is firmly ahead of him. His dynasty superflex value is up 460 points over 30 days, the largest rookie-back gain in the file.
13305.watch: Jeanty's workload. Washington is a dynasty stash more than a 2026 contributor.

11575.outlook: The primary insurance behind James Cook and one of the more valuable backups in the league given Buffalo's scoring environment. He handled seven touches in the preseason opener including four catches for 32 yards, which is the receiving usage that makes him relevant. Ty Johnson is also in the mix and is dealing with a knee issue. Only ESPN, FantasyPros and Fantasy Football Calculator ranked him.
11575.watch: A Cook injury. Buffalo's goal-line volume makes this handcuff more valuable than most.

11576.outlook: Played 28 percent of the Jets' snaps over the first three weeks of 2025 before a season-ending knee injury. He broke off a 31-yard touchdown run in the preseason. Breece Hall's groin strain, described as minor, is the immediate opening. He is a big back without much established receiving work.
11576.watch: Hall's groin. Allen is the direct beneficiary of any extended absence.

5995.outlook: Positioned for a larger role after Keaton Mitchell left, working as Baltimore's passing-down back behind Derrick Henry, who plays only about half the snaps. Reporting suggests Henry will be more involved in the passing game this year, which would cut into Hill's niche. FantasyPros has him RB71 against a consensus in the high 50s, a wide gap. He has no standalone rushing value.
5995.watch: Whether Henry actually absorbs the passing-down work; that is Hill's only source of value.

13337.outlook: A fifth-round rookie whose 3.4 career forced missed tackle rate was fourth best in his class. Jesse Newell of The Athletic indicated Johnson has been fourth in Kansas City's back pecking order behind Kenneth Walker III. He moved up 10 spots since the previous refresh but is still buried. Kansas City's offense would make any lead back valuable, which is why he retains some appeal.
13337.watch: Whether he climbs past Demercado and Brashard Smith for the No. 2 job.

12467.outlook: A fifth-round pick from 2025 who did not record a touch as a rookie, now a candidate to be 30-year-old Christian McCaffrey's primary backup. He missed the preseason opener with a ribs injury. McCaffrey has been managing tightness in camp, which raises the relevance of this role. FantasyPros has him RB73 with a 11.07 standard deviation, reflecting real disagreement.
12467.watch: McCaffrey's health. San Francisco has no established backup behind him.

11647.outlook: Third year with the Chargers, competing with Keaton Mitchell for change-of-pace touches behind Omarion Hampton. He started the preseason opener and managed five carries for eight yards. Mike McDaniel's hot-hand comment applies here as well. He had some productive stretches in 2025 when injuries opened the door.
11647.watch: A Hampton injury, and whether McDaniel favors him or Mitchell for the No. 2 role.

11643.outlook: Competing again with Ollie Gordon II for backup reps behind De'Von Achane. He has barely cleared 70 touches in either of his first two seasons. He rushed six times for 22 yards in the preseason. Miami's thin passing game means the run game matters, but Achane's workload leaves little behind him.
11643.watch: An Achane injury. Hafley's 40-touch comment about Achane makes the backup role low-value in normal weeks.

4147.outlook: Expected to resume his role as Chase Brown's primary backup, having played 31 percent of Cincinnati's snaps last season with 84 carries and 21 targets. At 30 he is a known quantity: a competent pass-blocker and receiver without standalone value. FantasyPros has him RB78 against a CBS and NBC consensus in the high 50s.
4147.watch: A Brown injury in a Bengals offense that will score plenty.

6039.outlook: The change-of-pace and receiving option behind James Cook, entering his eighth season having never cleared 63 carries. He left practice in early August with an apparent right knee injury and is listed as questionable. Ray Davis is the more likely beneficiary of a Cook absence. His value is almost entirely passing-down snaps.
6039.watch: The knee. He has a narrow role that does not survive an injury well.

4137.outlook: Entering his 10th season with no clear path to touches after a season-ending foot injury in Week 3 last year. Mike LaFleur said there is no timeline for Conner to participate in 11-on-11 drills. Arizona drafted Jeremiyah Love third overall and signed Tyler Allgeier. He is behind both on the depth chart.
4137.watch: Whether he is on the roster in September. The foot has kept him out of team drills entirely.

12457.outlook: A second-year back who logged 10 touches in the preseason, eight carries and two catches. He is behind Javonte Williams and Malik Davis in Dallas. FantasyPros has him RB66 with a 10.57 standard deviation. He offers receiving ability, which is the path to a role.
12457.watch: A Javonte Williams injury. Blue is the most explosive back in the Dallas room.

13414.outlook: A third-round rookie for San Francisco, a surprise selection given he failed to clear 190 touches in four college seasons. He missed the preseason opener with a thigh injury and is listed as questionable. He is behind McCaffrey and Jordan James. FantasyPros has him RB75 with a 12.27 standard deviation, one of the widest in the file.
13414.watch: Health and depth-chart position. He has not been on the field enough to establish either.

9506.outlook: Fourth year in Tampa Bay behind Bucky Irving and newly signed Kenny Gainwell. He managed 23 total yards on six touches in the preseason. Gainwell's arrival pushed him down the depth chart. He has flashed efficiency in limited work across his career.
9506.watch: Injuries ahead of him. He is third in a three-man room.

12048.outlook: On the fantasy radar with Kenneth Walker III gone and Zach Charbonnet on PUP with an ACL. He led Seattle's ground game in the preseason opener with 12 carries for 42 yards. Rookie first-rounder Jadarian Price is the projected starter. Seattle's run-first identity means volume exists if he wins snaps.
12048.watch: Whether he beats out Price for early-down work while Charbonnet is out.

12495.outlook: Battling Jaylen Wright for backup work behind De'Von Achane. He was used sparingly as a rookie and did not move the needle, but he rushed seven times for 39 yards in the preseason. Miami's offense is a question mark under Malik Willis. He is a bigger back than Wright, which may matter near the goal line.
12495.watch: An Achane injury, and whether Miami wants a bigger body in short yardage.

11571.outlook: Third-year Jets back who missed the preseason game with a knee injury and is listed as questionable. He is behind Breece Hall and Braelon Allen. His dynasty superflex value is up 302 points over 30 days, which likely reflects Hall's contract situation. He has limited established usage.
11571.watch: Injuries ahead of him. He is third in the Jets' backfield.

13405.outlook: A sixth-round rookie who saw a heavy preseason workload, rushing 23 times for 85 yards and a touchdown plus a catch. He ranked seventh in his class in YAC at 3.35. He is behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White in Washington. FantasyPros has him RB64 against a consensus in the low 70s.
13405.watch: Whether the preseason volume signals anything about the regular-season pecking order.

13288.outlook: A fifth-round rookie for Tennessee, a big versatile back with speed who can contribute as a rusher, receiver, blocker and returner. He led the Titans in carries in the preseason opener with eight. Tony Pollard missed a practice with an undisclosed issue and Tyjae Spears is the established backup. FantasyPros has him RB58, well ahead of the consensus, and he rose seven spots since the previous refresh.
13288.watch: Pollard's health. Singleton's skill set fits a three-down role if the opportunity comes.

11199.outlook: Listed as the No. 2 behind Kenneth Walker III in Kansas City, though reporting suggests the pecking order behind Walker is fluid with Brashard Smith and rookie Emmett Johnson also involved. He has no meaningful career production. Only the deeper sources ranked him. Kansas City's offense makes any real role valuable.
11199.watch: Whether he holds the No. 2 job through camp.

11435.outlook: Signed with Seattle and sat out the preseason opener with a hamstring injury. He is behind Jadarian Price, George Holani and a returning Zach Charbonnet in a crowded and unsettled backfield. His dynasty value is down 275 points over 30 days. He has limited career usage.
11435.watch: The hamstring, and whether he makes the roster in a crowded room.

11370.outlook: Third-year back in Green Bay behind Josh Jacobs and MarShawn Lloyd. He was not in uniform for the preseason opener. Jacobs' groin injury creates some opportunity but Lloyd has been getting the starts. He has minimal career production.
11370.watch: Roster status. He is third at best in this backfield.

13347.outlook: A sixth-round rookie for Minnesota who struggled badly with efficiency across four seasons at Wake Forest on 558 touches. He is behind Aaron Jones Sr. and Jordan Mason. FantasyPros has him RB69, ahead of the consensus. Minnesota's backfield is a committee of aging veterans, which is the argument for him.
13347.watch: Whether Jones' durability opens a path; the efficiency profile is a real concern.

12544.outlook: Out for the remainder of training camp with a soft-tissue injury sustained Monday, per the Jaguars. He played a modest role as a rookie and was competing with Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. for backfield work. The absence effectively removes him from the early-season competition. He had been getting third-down reps in scrimmages.
12544.watch: The injury timeline. He was the passing-down candidate before this.

13302.outlook: A fifth-round rookie for Baltimore, reportedly handpicked by owner Steve Bisciotti, and the biggest back in his class. He led the Ravens' ground attack in the preseason with 12 carries for 46 yards and a touchdown. Derrick Henry and Justice Hill are ahead of him. FantasyPros has him RB87, well behind the consensus.
13302.watch: Henry's age. Randall is a long-term contingency behind a 32-year-old workhorse.

12471.outlook: Second-year Colts back listed as the No. 2 behind Jonathan Taylor, currently dealing with a hamstring injury. Taylor's workload leaves little behind him in a normal week. Indianapolis' offense generates strong rushing volume, which makes the handcuff meaningful. He has limited established production.
12471.watch: Taylor's health. Giddens is the direct handcuff to a league-leading carry total.

12476.outlook: Second-year Saints back who missed the preseason opener with a hamstring injury. He is behind Travis Etienne Jr. and Alvin Kamara. Only FantasyPros and Fantasy Football Calculator ranked him, and he moved up 12 spots since the previous refresh. New Orleans' backfield could clarify if Kamara is phased out.
12476.watch: Kamara's status. Neal is third in a room that may become a two-man rotation.

6130.outlook: Veteran depth behind Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. in New York. He has been a competent committee back throughout his career but has no path to volume here. FantasyPros has him RB86. The Giants also worked out Najee Harris, which would further crowd the room.
6130.watch: Roster status. He is third in a backfield that just auditioned a fourth back.

12455.outlook: Second-year Chief competing with Emmett Johnson and Emari Demercado for the No. 2 job behind Kenneth Walker III. He played 17 percent of Kansas City's snaps as a rookie. A converted receiver, his path is passing-down work. The Kansas City offense makes even a modest role useful.
12455.watch: Whether he wins the passing-down job; that is where his skill set fits.

11577.outlook: Third-year Eagle behind Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby, who is nursing a toe injury. FantasyPros has him RB97, near the bottom of the ranked pool. He has minimal career production. Philadelphia's backfield is Barkley's by a wide margin.
11577.watch: Bigsby's toe, which would move Shipley to the top backup spot.

11588.outlook: Deep Houston depth dealing with a hip injury, behind David Montgomery and Woody Marks. FantasyPros has him RB103, the lowest ranking of any back in the file. He has no established NFL production. He is a roster-cut candidate.

7720.outlook: Ranked only by ESPN at RB91 and by no other source, which is why his sample size of one makes his placement unreliable. He is primarily a kick returner and is listed fifth on the Jets' depth chart. He has almost no offensive usage in his career. Treat the ranking as a return-game valuation rather than a fantasy one.
7720.watch: Nothing. He is a special-teams player in a fantasy file.

13424.outlook: A seventh-round rookie for Indianapolis who started the preseason opener with five carries for 17 yards and lost a fumble. He is an older prospect at 25 who bounced between five schools. He is behind Jonathan Taylor and DJ Giddens. FantasyPros has him RB83.
13424.watch: Roster status. He is competing for a practice-squad-to-roster spot.

11651.outlook: On the PUP list with a pectoral injury and listed as out. He is fifth on San Francisco's depth chart behind McCaffrey, Jordan James and Kaelon Black. He flashed genuine explosiveness when given chances in 2024. FantasyPros has him RB94.
11651.watch: Clearance from PUP. He cannot be evaluated until he practices.

7528.outlook: Listed with the Chargers in Sleeper but is effectively a free agent - John Harbaugh said Harris, working back from an Achilles injury, looked good in a Monday workout with the Giants. Only FantasyPros ranked him, at RB93, which is why his average is unreliable. He has been a high-volume, low-efficiency back throughout his career. His team designation in this file is stale.
7528.watch: Where he signs. Landing spot determines everything for him.

1379.outlook: A fullback, filed at running back per Sleeper's position mapping, dealing with a finger injury. He has no fantasy relevance in standard formats. FantasyPros has him RB112 with a standard deviation of 21.93, by far the widest in the file, which reflects that most rankers do not rate fullbacks at all. He is in the file only because the depth targets extend to 100 backs.
1379.watch: Nothing. He is a blocking specialist.

8800.outlook: Listed as the No. 2 behind Javonte Williams in Dallas. He has minimal career production across four seasons. His dynasty value is down 202 points over 30 days. He is a depth piece rather than a genuine handcuff.
8800.watch: Whether Dallas adds a back; the current room behind Williams is thin.

9757.outlook: Missed the preseason game with a back injury and is listed as questionable. He is fifth on the Saints' depth chart behind Etienne, Kamara and Devin Neal. Injuries have defined his career. He has flashed talent in very limited healthy windows.
9757.watch: Health. He has not strung together a healthy stretch since being drafted.

11569.outlook: Second-year Rams back behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum. Only FantasyPros and Fantasy Football Calculator ranked him. He has limited established usage. Los Angeles' backfield is settled at the top two spots.
11569.watch: Injuries ahead of him. He is third in a clear hierarchy.

13348.outlook: An undrafted or late-round rookie listed fourth on Jacksonville's depth chart. LeQuint Allen's camp-ending injury opens a small window. FantasyPros has him RB106, near the bottom of the file. He has no NFL production.
13348.watch: Roster status in a crowded and unsettled Jaguars backfield.

12472.outlook: Second-year Browns back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. Only two sources ranked him and they disagree by 20 spots, so his placement is unstable. He has minimal career usage. Cleveland's offense is unlikely to support a third back.

12738.outlook: Dealing with a chest injury, though Brian Schottenheimer said after the preseason game that Mafah will be OK. He is fifth on the Cowboys' depth chart. FantasyPros has him RB105 with a 15.55 standard deviation. He has no meaningful NFL production.

12531.outlook: Second-year Panthers back listed fourth on the depth chart behind Chuba Hubbard and Jonathon Brooks. Hubbard's hamstring creates some theoretical opportunity. FantasyPros has him RB90. He has limited career usage.
12531.watch: Whether Carolina's backfield injuries cascade far enough down to reach him.

8122.outlook: Fifth on Arizona's depth chart. Only ESPN and FantasyPros ranked him and they disagree by eight spots. Jeremiyah Love's ankle and James Conner's foot have thinned the room, which is likely why he appears at all. He has minimal career production.
8122.watch: Whether Arizona's injuries open a roster spot.

12543.outlook: Second-year Bengals back listed third behind Chase Brown and Samaje Perine. His dynasty value is down 241 points over 30 days. FantasyPros has him RB95. Cincinnati's offense concentrates backfield work heavily in Brown.
12543.watch: Roster status behind an established top two.

7564.outlook: Six of seven sources have him WR1 and his 0.37 standard deviation at FantasyPros is the tightest of any skill player in the file. He has finished four of five seasons no worse than fifth in points per game. His yardage dipped from 1,740 to 1,426 in 2025 largely because Joe Burrow missed nine games. Burrow is back and healthy, and Cincinnati is installing an offense that camp reporting describes as coming together.
7564.watch: Burrow's availability. Chase's floor with a backup quarterback is meaningfully lower and he has now lived through it.
