9493.outlook: Has finished each of his three seasons sixth or better among receivers, an extraordinary run for a fifth-round pick. He has a groin injury and Sean McVay said he may not practice at all this week, which is the most consequential injury situation for any player ranked this highly. Matthew Stafford is coming off an MVP season and Davante Adams remains the red-zone target. His redraft market value is down 255 points over 30 days.
9493.watch: The groin. Soft-tissue injuries in mid-August routinely bleed into September.

9488.outlook: The reigning Offensive Player of the Year led all receivers in target share at 36 percent, receiving yards at 1,793, air yards and yards per route run at 3.8. That target share is the highest in the league and is the entire investment case. Seattle's run-first identity under Brian Fleury is the mild concern, though it did not stop him last year. Sam Darnold returns at quarterback.
9488.watch: Whether Fleury's scheme preserves the volume; nothing about the talent is in doubt.

7547.outlook: The only player in NFL history with 90-plus catches in each of his first five seasons and has finished exactly third among receivers repeatedly. Dan Campbell has called this the best receiver room he has had, which is a mild negative for target concentration. Jared Goff's volume is reliable and the slot role insulates him from coverage. All seven sources have him WR4.
7547.watch: Target share erosion if Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa both take a step forward.

6786.outlook: Finished 12th among receivers in points per game in 2025, his worst mark since 2021, though he still cleared 1,000 yards for a fifth straight season while missing three games. George Pickens' arrival is the complicating factor for target share, but Pickens also draws coverage away. Lamb has said he and Prescott are hitting on all cylinders in camp. Dallas will throw enough to support both.
6786.watch: The Pickens split. Lamb's 2025 dip coincided with a lower target share, not a talent decline.

6794.outlook: Plummeted to 30th among receivers in points per game in 2025, entirely a function of Minnesota's quarterback problems rather than anything he did. Kyler Murray was named the Week 1 starter, which is a substantial upgrade and the main reason to buy back in. Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson return around him. Camp reporting indicates he and Murray are starting to click.
6794.watch: Murray's health and the Vikings' offensive line, which caused the 2025 collapse in the first place.

8112.outlook: Broke out with a 100-1,271-9 line and a fifth-place finish in points per game, and is aiming for a third straight top-15 season. Kevin Stefanski is the new head coach and Tua Tagovailoa is the quarterback, both changes from last year. The receiver room behind him is thin, which concentrates targets. Sources are tight at WR7 except Fantasy Football Calculator at WR5.
8112.watch: Tagovailoa's arm strength on the deep and contested throws London wins.

7569.outlook: Has cleared 1,000 yards and scored seven or eight touchdowns in each of the past two seasons without ever playing a full 17-game slate. Camp reporting says he has been in top form. C.J. Stroud's declining production every year is the drag on his outlook, not anything about Collins. Jayden Higgins opposite him should draw some coverage.
7569.watch: Games played, and whether Stroud's regression finally stops.

10229.outlook: Still looking for his first full season as a starter after injury in 2024 and a six-game suspension plus injury in 2025. Ian Rapoport reported he is unlikely to face further league discipline for a probation violation, which removes the biggest overhang. Patrick Mahomes' ACL recovery is the new variable. FantasyPros' 3.57 standard deviation on him is among the widest in the top 20.
10229.watch: Mahomes' Week 1 status. Rice's ceiling is directly tied to it.

5859.outlook: Traded to New England in June and has been the clear No. 1 option in joint practices. He has finished top 15 in points per game in each of his four Eagles seasons. Drake Maye led the league in completion percentage and yards per attempt last year, so the quarterback play is an upgrade over what Philadelphia offered late. His redraft market value is up 567 points over 30 days, the largest gain of any receiver.
5859.watch: Chemistry timing with Maye and the age-29 curve; the situation itself is excellent.

8137.outlook: Franchise-tagged after a career year in which he ranked near the top of the position in catches, yards, touchdowns, end-zone targets - second with 18 - and air yards. He has been dominant throughout Dallas' camp. CeeDee Lamb is the alpha but Pickens' red-zone role is his own. His redraft market value is down 434 points over 30 days despite no negative news.
8137.watch: Whether the 18 end-zone targets repeat; that volume drove most of his touchdown total.

8144.outlook: Career year in 2025 with highs in targets at 156, receptions at 100, yardage at 1,163 and touchdowns at nine, finishing eighth among receivers in points per game. Rookie Jordyn Tyson is expected to miss roughly two months with a hamstring, which keeps Olave as the unambiguous No. 1 target. Tyler Shough returns after a strong second half. His market value is up 671 points in redraft over 30 days, the largest positive move in the receiver file.
8144.watch: Concussion history. It has cost him significant time in prior seasons.

11632.outlook: Logged his first 11-on-11 reps in a red non-contact jersey on August 17, coming off the torn ACL that limited him to four games. Across 18 full career games he has a 35 percent target share at 11.3 per game and averages 18.2 points. He moved up five spots since the previous refresh as the recovery progressed. Jaxson Dart, Isaiah Likely and Darnell Mooney fill out an improved offense under Matt Nagy.
11632.watch: Full clearance for contact. The target share is elite; the knee is the only question.

9997.outlook: Set career bests in target share at 29 percent, targets at 118, catches at 86 and yardage at 1,211 in 2025. He still lacks a role near the goal line, which caps the touchdown upside. He participated in team drills after a quadriceps issue and was rested for the preseason opener. Baltimore's new staff under Jesse Minter is the unknown.
9997.watch: Red-zone usage. Everything else about his profile has already improved.

7525.outlook: Has finished no lower than 30th among receivers while playing second fiddle to A.J. Brown, and Brown is now in New England. That makes him the clear No. 1 target in Philadelphia for the first time. He has a hamstring injury but appeared prepared to practice on August 17 and went through warmups before the preseason game. Sean Mannion is the new playcaller.
7525.watch: The hamstring first, then whether Hurts' passing volume holds without Brown drawing coverage.

8146.outlook: Limited to seven games in 2025 after appearing in all 51 during his first three seasons. He missed a day with a stomach bug and returned to practice Tuesday, so the illness is a non-issue. Geno Smith is an upgrade over what the Jets ran out last year. His talent has never been the question - the quarterback play has.
8146.watch: Whether Geno Smith is actually good enough to support a WR1 season.

6801.outlook: Has missed seven games over the past two seasons but plays a key role near the goal line in a pass-friendly offense. Camp reporting says he and Burrow have had no trouble connecting. Ja'Marr Chase absorbs the coverage attention, which is why Higgins' efficiency stays high. He is the WR2 on his own team and still a weekly starter.
6801.watch: Availability. His per-game production is well established; his games-played column is not.

12526.outlook: The reigning Offensive Rookie of the Year and a candidate to enter the elite tier. He was top 15 among receivers in snaps and volume as a rookie and Dave Canales said he got bigger and stronger this offseason. Bryce Young is the limiting factor and has been for three years. He is the WR10 in the dynasty superflex market, well ahead of his redraft rank.
12526.watch: Bryce Young. McMillan's ceiling is capped by the worst quarterback situation of any top-20 receiver.

12514.outlook: Todd Bowles called him day-to-day to week-to-week with a toe sprain and was non-committal about Week 1, though the team was earlier described as optimistic after tests confirmed the sprain is stable. His rookie season split sharply: five touchdowns and 20.5 points per game over the first five games, then one touchdown and 7.8 points over the final stretch. Chris Godwin's return complicates the target share. Tampa Bay's offense has a new coordinator in Zac Robinson.
12514.watch: The toe. Bowles' language moved from optimistic to non-committal within a week.

11635.outlook: Dipped from an 82-1,155-7 rookie line and a 12th-place finish to 66 catches in 2025. Mike McDaniel is the new coordinator, which is a scheme change that should suit a separator working the slot. Justin Herbert has a healthy offensive line for the first time in years. He said in late July he would be full go for camp after a hamstring issue.
11635.watch: Whether McDaniel's system restores his target volume; the talent is not in question.

7526.outlook: Traded to Denver after five seasons in Miami, where he finished top 30 in points per game four times without reaching a higher gear. He returned to practice on August 17 after a leg issue. Davis Webb is the new Denver playcaller and Bo Nix's deep accuracy has drawn praise in camp. Courtland Sutton is the incumbent and Waddle is listed as the RWR1.
7526.watch: How Denver splits targets between him and Sutton; both are being paid like No. 1 receivers.

5927.outlook: Coming off a lost 2025 in which he missed seven games and Jayden Daniels missed 10. At 30 he remains Washington's clear No. 1 target, though the team signed Stefon Diggs in August. David Blough is the new playcaller. The 2024 version of this offense with a healthy Daniels produced a strong McLaurin season.
5927.watch: Daniels' health, which drives everything in this passing game.

2133.outlook: Led all receivers in touchdowns for the third time in six seasons in his first Rams year, with 27 end-zone targets - nine more than any other player. At 33 the volume is the risk, not the role. Puka Nacua's groin injury could push more targets his way early. He was rested for the preseason opener.
2133.watch: Age-related decline in separation, which would show up first in the end-zone target count.

4983.outlook: Traded to Buffalo, where he becomes Josh Allen's first true No. 1 receiver. He was reduced to a 16 percent target share in 2025, his lowest since his rookie year, in a crowded Chicago room. He is dealing with a lower-body issue but practiced Tuesday and said he was good to go. FantasyPros' 4.96 standard deviation reflects real disagreement about how Buffalo distributes targets.
4983.watch: The lower-body injury, and whether Buffalo actually funnels volume to him over Shakir and Kincaid.

12519.outlook: One of the most popular breakout picks in fantasy after flashing elite efficiency in limited rookie work. He played sparingly for most of 2025 behind Rome Odunze and is listed as the RWR2. He is managing a lower-body issue. Ben Johnson's offense and Caleb Williams' development are the supporting arguments.
12519.watch: Snap share. The efficiency is proven; the playing time is not.

8148.outlook: Back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons after a slow start to his career, setting new highs in 2025 following a 22nd-place fantasy finish in 2024. He is dealing with a minor shoulder injury and was rested in the preseason opener. Amon-Ra St. Brown absorbs the target volume, which caps Williams' floor. His profile is big-play dependent.
8148.watch: The shoulder, and whether Detroit's expanded receiver room cuts into his targets.

11620.outlook: Opened 2025 with five touchdowns in his first four games and 15-plus points in each, then collapsed to one touchdown the rest of the way. He is listed as the LWR1 ahead of Luther Burden III. His redraft market value is down 434 points over 30 days. Ben Johnson's offense supports multiple receivers but Burden and Colston Loveland are both trending up.
11620.watch: Whether the target hierarchy in Chicago settles on him or Burden.

2216.outlook: Signed with San Francisco at 32 after his streak of 11 straight 1,000-yard seasons ended with a nine-game absence. He participated in team drills on August 15 after a quadriceps issue. Brock Purdy is healthy and Kyle Shanahan's offense generates efficient target distribution. ESPN and CBS both like him more than his ADP of 95 suggests.
2216.watch: Health at 32, and whether Deebo Samuel's return splits the outside targets.

8167.outlook: A genuinely boom-bust profile - he missed the first seven games of 2025, then scored 18-plus points four times but averaged 7.7 in his other six. He is listed as Green Bay's LWR1. His redraft market value is up 358 points over 30 days. Jordan Love's efficiency is excellent even if the volume is not.
8167.watch: Health. He has never played a full season.

9487.outlook: A strong finish to 2025 made him one of the more interesting breakout candidates, though he is considered day-to-day with an undisclosed injury and sat out the preseason opener. He is listed as Jacksonville's slot starter. His market value is up 527 points in redraft over 30 days, a substantial move. Travis Hunter moving primarily to defense clears targets for him.
9487.watch: The undisclosed injury, and whether the late-2025 usage carries over.

11628.outlook: Serviceable as a rookie with 885 yards and eight touchdowns but missed five games and has been limited since. He caught a touchdown in the preseason opener and drew a 20-yard pass interference penalty. Jacoby Brissett is the quarterback, which caps the ceiling. His redraft market value is down 370 points over 30 days.
11628.watch: Whether the fourth-overall-pick talent finally shows up; two seasons in it has not.

11631.outlook: One of the biggest wildcards in the file. He was fantasy's WR4 as a rookie but only produced at that level with Mac Jones under center, and Jacksonville envisions him as the X receiver this year. Trevor Lawrence is coming off his best season. Sources cluster at WR30-33 but the range of outcomes is unusually wide.
11631.watch: Whether Lawrence can support him the way Jones did; that split is the whole evaluation.

13279.outlook: The fourth overall pick, coming off a college career with the best yards per target in his class at 13.1 and 3.06 yards per route run. Robert Saleh said he will be evaluated after taking a hard hit at Monday's practice. He is Tennessee's LWR1 and had a standout camp session in early August. He is the WR12 in the dynasty superflex market, far ahead of his redraft rank.
13279.watch: The hit he took Monday, and whether Cam Ward can support a rookie's target volume.

5846.outlook: Mike McCarthy said he will be hard pressed to work in practice, and he did not suit up for the preseason opener with an undisclosed issue. His first Pittsburgh season was solid but unspectacular - two missed games and a career-low 850 yards. Aaron Rodgers returns at 42. Michael Pittman Jr. is also banged up, which concentrates targets if Metcalf is healthy.
5846.watch: The undisclosed injury. Neither he nor Pittman has been able to practice.

5045.outlook: Two straight seasons of 1,000 yards and top-20 fantasy finishes after only one in his first six years. Denver traded for Jaylen Waddle, which is a direct threat to his target share, and Sutton is now listed as the LWR2. He caught all three targets for 60 yards in the preseason. His target share had already dipped before Waddle arrived.
5045.watch: The Waddle split. Denver now has two receivers who need volume to justify their contracts.

10232.outlook: Broke out over the final eight games of 2025 with Jacoby Brissett under center, averaging 11.0 targets and 21.2 fantasy points after averaging 4.3 and 7.6 across his first 38 games. Brissett is again the starter, which is why the breakout may be repeatable. Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride are ahead of him in the pecking order. FantasyPros' 5.93 standard deviation reflects genuine disagreement.
10232.watch: Whether the eight-game sample was real. It is the single most extreme split in the receiver file.

8142.outlook: On PUP with an ankle injury and Shane Steichen does not expect him back during joint practices, though GM Chris Ballard said he is expected to play Week 1. He became one of the league's highest-paid receivers this offseason despite four years as a situational deep threat. Indianapolis signed Keenan Allen in August. His market value is down 254 points in redraft over 30 days.
8142.watch: The ankle. A PUP designation with a Week 1 target is a narrow window.

4037.outlook: Limited to 16 games over two seasons and reached 11 fantasy points only twice in nine appearances in 2025. He sat out the first preseason game. Emeka Egbuka's toe injury could open early volume. His ADP of 148 is far below his WR34 consensus, which is the clearest value gap in the receiver file.
4037.watch: Health. The role is available if he can hold up.

9500.outlook: Has finished between 35th and 45th among receivers in total points in each of his three seasons, peaking with a 72-803-5 line in 2024. He briefly left practice after a hard fall on his back but returned and was cleared. Indianapolis signed Keenan Allen, another slot-capable target. Daniel Jones' efficiency supports him.
9500.watch: The Allen signing, which is a direct threat to his slot snaps.

6819.outlook: Traded to Pittsburgh after handling 23.6 percent of Indianapolis' targets over six seasons and four top-20 fantasy campaigns. Mike McCarthy said he will be hard pressed to practice with a leg injury, alongside DK Metcalf. He did not play in the preseason opener. Aaron Rodgers is the quarterback.
6819.watch: The leg injury. Both Pittsburgh starters have missed the same practice windows.

9756.outlook: His targets, receptions, yardage and touchdowns have all declined in each of the past two seasons after a 70-911-10 rookie year. 8210.watch: Whether Washington's offense elevates him past the low-end TE1 range he has occupied.

5001.outlook: One of the league's most consistent tight ends but useful in fantasy only once, when he was TE3 in Dallas in 2021; he has finished 10th or worse in his other eight seasons. C.J. Stroud's declining production caps him. CBS's Cummings is a clear outlier at TE13 while Richard has him 30th. He did not play in the preseason opener.
5001.watch: Nothing structural. He is a floor play with an established low ceiling.

5844.outlook: Has not recovered his 2023 form since tearing an ACL, posting a 16 percent target share in 2025, his lowest. Kyler Murray taking over should improve the passing game meaningfully. ESPN is highest at TE14 while the CBS trio has him TE23-29, the widest source gap among mid-range tight ends. He played five snaps in the preseason.
5844.watch: Whether Murray's arrival restores his target share; the sources are deeply split on it.

8172.outlook: Back on the fantasy radar as the top tight end on Miami's depth chart, having flashed as a Denver rookie with a 33-411-2 line before totaling 16 targets across two seasons. He played 13 snaps in the preseason without a stat line. FantasyPros has him TE36 while CBS's Richard has him TE16, one of the widest disagreements in the file at 5.44 standard deviation. Miami's passing game under Malik Willis is a real constraint.
8172.watch: Whether being TE1 on a thin depth chart means anything in an offense with this quarterback.

13330.outlook: The 16th overall pick, working on a side field with a hernia as of August 18 and listed as questionable with an abdomen issue. He broke out in college with a 51-560-8 line on a 17 percent target share and aligned in the slot 62 percent of the time. ESPN is aggressive at TE17 while the CBS trio has him TE24-28. He is the TE9 in dynasty superflex, far ahead of his redraft rank.
13330.watch: The hernia. Rookie tight ends who miss August rarely contribute in September.

11603.outlook: Worked his way to the top of Seattle's depth chart and found the end zone seven times, finishing 14th in fantasy points despite ranking 20th among tight ends in targets and yards. That is a touchdown-dependent profile. He was rested in the preseason opener. Seattle's run-first offense limits the volume available.
11603.watch: Touchdown regression. His underlying usage does not support last year's finish.

12493.outlook: A roller-coaster rookie season: 29.4 points in Week 7 and 18.7 in Week 8, then one touchdown and 6.2 points per game the rest of the way with no game above 12.2. He caught two of three targets in the preseason. The Chargers signed David Njoku, which complicates the role. NBC has him TE15 while ESPN has him 32nd and CBS's Richard 31st - the widest spread of any tight end.
12493.watch: The Njoku signing. Los Angeles added a veteran directly on top of him.

7600.outlook: Flirted with TE1 status in 2022 and 2024 but saw a dramatic usage dip in Pittsburgh's crowded 2025 offense. He caught his only target for two yards in the preseason. Both starting receivers are banged up, which could funnel targets his way early. Only four sources ranked him.
7600.watch: Whether the Metcalf and Pittman injuries create early-season volume.

12487.outlook: A breakout candidate in Year 2 after a situational rookie role behind Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen, used almost exclusively as a vertical threat. He was a standout in the Rams' joint practice with Dallas. He is now listed as the starter with Parkinson second. ESPN is highest at TE19 while Fantasy Football Calculator has him 33rd.
12487.watch: Whether he holds the starting job; the Rams have rotated tight ends heavily.

12502.outlook: Caught 44 passes as a rookie, 11th among rookie tight ends over the past decade, while playing behind Chig Okonkwo, and caught 79 percent of his 56 targets. Okonkwo left for Washington, making Helm the starter. He caught his only target for 16 yards in the preseason. Cam Ward's development is the constraint.
12502.watch: Whether Tennessee's offense improves enough to support a fantasy-relevant tight end.

8111.outlook: Re-signed with Tampa Bay and ranks first among all tight ends in snaps since 2022 and second in routes, which has never translated to target volume - he has not cleared 86 targets in a season. He did not play in the preseason opener. Zac Robinson is the new coordinator. Only four sources ranked him.
8111.watch: Whether the new scheme finally converts his snap volume into targets.

4066.outlook: Underwhelming first Denver season with a career-low 13 percent target share and finishes of 15th or worse among tight ends in routes, targets, catches and yardage despite 16 games. Denver added Jaylen Waddle, further crowding the target picture. He is 31. His dynasty value at TE41 is far below his TE30 redraft rank.
4066.watch: Whether Davis Webb's offense uses the tight end at all.

2505.outlook: Signed a one-year deal with Carolina in mid-August and did not practice Monday as the team eases him in; he was reported with a groin issue at signing. He is listed atop Carolina's tight end depth chart, which drives his TE31 blend rank. FantasyPros has him TE50 while CBS's Richard has him TE17 - a 7.98 standard deviation, the widest of any player in the file. His dynasty value is up 606 points over 30 days on the signing news.
2505.watch: Whether he plays at all. The sources have not converged because the signing is days old.

4033.outlook: Signed with the Chargers after nine seasons in Cleveland. He has not played a full season since 2018 and is coming off a lost 2025, but was a productive fantasy starter in the years before that. He is listed second behind Oronde Gadsden II. Only four sources ranked him.
4033.watch: Whether he passes Gadsden for the starting job; the Chargers signed him for a reason.

6865.outlook: From Week 10 onward last season, including playoffs, he averaged 5.0 targets and 12.1 fantasy points across 12 games, a genuinely useful stretch. He is now listed second behind Terrance Ferguson in the Rams' tight end committee. Only four sources ranked him. Los Angeles rotates this position heavily.
6865.watch: Whether the second-half 2025 role returns or Ferguson takes it.

4993.outlook: Has finished 23rd, 37th, 13th and 41st among tight ends over the past four seasons after two top-eight campaigns in 2020 and 2021. He is nominally atop Cincinnati's depth chart, which says more about the room than about him. He did not catch his only preseason target. Only three sources ranked him.
4993.watch: Nothing. Cincinnati concentrates targets in Chase, Higgins and Chase Brown.

9482.outlook: Entering a contract year as the No. 2 tight end behind Brock Bowers, a role that produced 2.9 targets and 3.4 fantasy points per game last season. He has never come close to a full season. Only four sources ranked him. Las Vegas' quarterback situation is unresolved.
9482.watch: A Bowers injury. He has no standalone path.

8698.outlook: On the fantasy radar because George Kittle is on PUP with a torn Achilles, which makes Tonges the 49ers' top tight end while Kittle is out. Kittle said he is confident he will be available early, which would end this window quickly. Only three sources ranked him and CBS's Richard has him TE25 against a consensus in the mid-30s. He is a new entrant to the ranked pool.
8698.watch: Kittle's PUP status. Tonges is a pure contingency play with a possibly very short window.

11533.outlook: The consensus K1 with the tightest agreement at the position, a 0.42 standard deviation at FantasyPros. He is perfect on his preseason attempts so far. Dallas' offense generates high scoring volume with Prescott, Lamb and Pickens, and Aubrey's range gives him a scoring profile no other kicker matches. Only the Rutgers and Patty'sBaddies leagues use kickers.
11533.watch: Nothing meaningful. He is the one kicker worth taking early.

3451.outlook: Ranks second in the blend at 32 with a settled job in Houston. CBS's Richard has him K1 while ESPN has him fifth. Houston's offense has been mediocre under C.J. Stroud, which limits attempts but also produces more field goal opportunities in the red zone. He did not kick in the preseason opener.
3451.watch: Houston's red-zone efficiency, which cuts both ways for a kicker.

8259.outlook: Entering his fifth season and fourth as the Chargers' undisputed starter. He has been among the league's most accurate kickers. Los Angeles' offense should improve with a healthy line and Mike McDaniel's scheme. Sources place him between K2 and K5.
8259.watch: Nothing. Job security and accuracy are both established.

2747.outlook: Entering his 12th season with a secure job in Seattle. He missed his only field goal attempt from 45 yards in the preseason opener. Seattle's run-first offense produces steady red-zone trips that often stall, which is favorable for kicker volume. Fantasy Football Calculator has him K2.
2747.watch: Age-35 leg strength on long attempts.

11786.outlook: Made all three field goal attempts and his extra point in the preseason opener. He has one of the strongest legs in the league at 23. Jacksonville's offense under Liam Coen with a healthy Trevor Lawrence should generate volume. Sources agree tightly at K4-9.
11786.watch: Nothing. He is the youngest kicker in the top tier with a secure job.

5189.outlook: Holds the San Francisco job in an offense that should score frequently with a healthy Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey and an upgraded receiver room. Sources are tight at K6-7 except Fantasy Football Calculator at 15. He has been a competent if unspectacular kicker.
5189.watch: Job security; San Francisco has changed kickers more than most teams.

12711.outlook: Second-year Baltimore kicker in an offense that reliably produces scoring opportunities with Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry. CBS's Richard has him K18 against a consensus around K7, the widest disagreement at the position. Baltimore's new coaching staff is a mild unknown.
12711.watch: The source disagreement; one CBS ranker sees a job-security risk the others do not.

12015.outlook: Made both field goals and both extra points in the Rams' preseason win. ESPN has him K4 while CBS's Cummings has him 17th, a wide split. The Rams' offense with Matthew Stafford should produce plenty of attempts. He is entering his second season.
12015.watch: Job security. The source spread suggests the role is not universally viewed as settled.

11539.outlook: Detroit's kicker in one of the league's higher-scoring offenses, which is the main argument for him. Fantasy Football Calculator has him K5 while CBS's Eisenberg has him 16th. He has a strong leg. He rose into the top 10 this refresh.
11539.watch: Accuracy consistency, which is why the sources are split on him.

7839.outlook: A new entrant to the top 10 this refresh, replacing Chase McLaughlin. Cincinnati's offense with a healthy Joe Burrow should generate substantial scoring volume. CBS's Richard has him K5 while ESPN has him 15th and Fantasy Football Calculator 17th. His accuracy has been inconsistent in recent seasons.
7839.watch: Accuracy. The offense will give him chances; converting them has been the issue.
